summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, recurrent UTIs, and chronic pain, was admitted for dysuria. He was found to have a Group B Streptococcus urinary tract infection based on an outside culture. He was started on IV linezolid and later transitioned to oral cephalexin given his allergies. Blood cultures were negative, and a renal ultrasound showed no hydronephrosis or structural abnormalities. He remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable throughout the admission. His home medications, including immunosuppressants and pain regimens, were continued. He was discharged home with a 14-day course of cephalexin, instructions to complete the antibiotics, and plans for a follow-up urine culture and urology evaluation to address recurrent infections.
